bib.title: TrueTeacher: Learning Factual Consistency Evaluation with Large Language Models

question: Can annotating real model-generated summaries with an LLM produce synthetic training data that makes a small NLI-style model a better, more domain-robust factual consistency evaluator than perturbation-based synthetic data?
hypothesis: A strong LLM can label model-generated summaries with sufficient quality to train a student that beats perturbation-based synthetic data and generalizes out of domain.
contributions: TrueTeacher: synthetic data by annotating model-generated summaries with an LLM
Evaluation of FLAN-PaLM 540B on factual consistency, distilled into a smaller model
Systematic re-evaluation of existing synthetic data methods under controlled conditions
First multilingual synthetic data experiment for factual consistency
Release of 1.4M example dataset and a checkpoint

method.summary: Fine-tune T5 (small to 11B) summarizers on XSum, summarize CNN/DM training documents, label each document-summary pair consistent/inconsistent with zero-shot FLAN-PaLM 540B, then train a T5 student classifier on the labels (alone or mixed with ANLI). Compare against FactEdit, DocNLI, FactCC and Falsesum data under matched size and a CNN/DM-only, out-of-domain test.
method.task: factual consistency evaluation of summaries (binary classification, distillation from LLM labels)

datasets.name: TrueTeacher synthetic data
datasets.split: CNN/DM training set documents only, gold summaries unused; full-data run balances labels by sampling 475,563 positive examples; study runs use 100k balanced examples
datasets.preprocessing: FLAN-PaLM answers 'It's impossible to say' are discarded

datasets.name: XSum
datasets.split: training set for summarizers; dev ROUGE as stopping criterion

datasets.name: TRUE summarization subset (MNBM, FRANK, SummEval, QAGS-X, QAGS-C)
datasets.preprocessing: FRANK split into FRANK-C (CNN/DM) and FRANK-X (XSum) for domain analysis

datasets.name: FactCC dataset (dev set for prompt and checkpoint selection)
datasets.split: dev and test merged, following Utama et al. 2022

datasets.name: WikiLingua (multilingual documents)
datasets.size: 100k sampled: 25k per language (en, es, fr, de), 12,500 consistent + 12,500 inconsistent each

datasets.name: mFACE test set
datasets.preprocessing: average attribution score >0.5 treated as consistent

other.also: T5-base used for the smaller-capacity study

other.uses: multilingual summarizer (XLSum) and multilingual student (ANLI+XNLI baseline)

training.objective: binary classification: predict '1' if summary is factually consistent, '0' otherwise; input 'Premise: {document} Hypothesis: {summary}'
training.steps: checkpoint evaluated every 1k steps; best-ROC-AUC checkpoint on dev
training.seq_len: 512 tokens max input in training (premise truncated); 2048 at inference

other.summarizer_training: T5 models fine-tuned on XSum 'in a similar fashion', ROUGE on XSum dev as stopping criterion
other.same_regime: same training regime used for all baselines

inference.decoding: FLAN-PaLM label: predict mode, 'Yes' -> consistent, 'No' -> inconsistent; ROC-AUC score = probability of generating 'Yes' (score mode)
inference.prompting: zero-shot NLI-style prompt for the teacher

parameters.self_verification_filter: tried and dropped; removed 15% of data

metrics.name: ROC-AUC
metrics.definition: binary classification setting on TRUE benchmark datasets, averaged across datasets

metrics.name: Labeling accuracy (human)
metrics.definition: binary attribution judgement by NLP researchers on 100 sampled examples (50 pos, 50 neg)

metrics.name: Abstractiveness (coverage x density)
metrics.definition: Grusky et al. 2018 extractive fragment coverage times density, on 5k random examples

eval.protocol: Study restricts each method to 100k balanced examples, CNN/DM-based only; CNN/DM test sets in-domain, XSum-based out-of-domain; repeated with T5-base and with/without ANLI. Single runs; no seeds or significance tests stated. Human eval: one rater per example, NLP researchers with 1+ year experience, max 10 examples each.

prompts.text: Premise: {document} Hypothesis: {summary} Can the hypothesis be inferred from the premise? Answer using "Yes" or "No" only.
Premise: {document} Hypothesis: {summary} Are you sure that the summary can be inferred from the document? Answer using "Yes" or "No" only.

results.claim: T5-11B trained on ANLI plus the full TrueTeacher data sets a new state of the art on the TRUE summarization subset and beats its 540B teacher.
results.setup: T5-11B, ANLI + full ~1.4M TrueTeacher, five TRUE summarization datasets
results.quote: improves a state-of-the-art model’s ROC-AUC from 82.7 to 87.8

results.claim: FLAN-PaLM 540B zero-shot is itself a strong consistency evaluator, on par with the Ensemble.
results.quote: FLAN-PaLM 540B achieves an impressive performance, with an average ROC-AUC of 84.9 compared to 83.0 of the best single-model baseline

results.claim: Out of domain (XSum documents), TrueTeacher is the only method above its ANLI-only baseline; Falsesum collapses.
results.metric: out-of-domain average ROC-AUC, T5-11B, 100k examples, no ANLI
results.setup: T5-11B, 100k CNN/DM-based examples, XSum-based test sets
results.table: Table 3, row TrueTeacher (T5-11B), column Out-of-domain: 85.7 (+0.7); Falsesum 69.7 (-15.3)

results.claim: TrueTeacher-only T5-11B with 100k examples already matches the 540B teacher on TRUE.
results.quote: the TrueTeacher-based variant using T5-11B (85.2) already performs on-par with the 540B LLM teacher (84.9, Table 2)

results.claim: Scaling from 100k to the full dataset improves TrueTeacher + ANLI.
In-domain, mixing ANLI with Falsesum or TrueTeacher raises the T5-11B in-domain score.
Human labeling accuracy of the synthetic data is 89%; the LLM labels are high precision on the inconsistent class and weaker on consistent.
results.setup: 100 examples (50 positive, 50 negative), NLP researcher raters
results.quote: The labeling accuracy of the sampled examples from our data stands at 89%
results.note: Table 4: consistent precision 80.0 recall 97.6; inconsistent precision 98.0 recall 83.1

results.claim: Better labels and model-generated summaries contribute about equally; both together give the best result.
results.quote:
label correctness and summary distribution have a similar effect on the perfor-
mance
results.table: Table 5, rows Falsesum + ANLI, TrueTeacher + ANLI, LabelAblation, SummaryAblation

results.claim: Filtering with self-verification raised label accuracy about 5% but did not improve the student.
results.quote: we got an average of 86 ROC-AUC on TRUE using the ﬁltered data, slightly below the 86.4 using the unﬁltered data

results.claim: Zero-shot, few-shot and chain-of-thought prompting of FLAN-PaLM give nearly the same dev accuracy, so zero-shot was used.
results.table: Table 8, row zero-shot, column Dev accuracy

results.claim: TrueTeacher summaries are the most abstractive among compared methods.
results.setup: random sample of 5k examples per method

results.claim: Adding multilingual TrueTeacher data improves mFACE ROC-AUC over ANLI+XNLI and beats the English-only variant.
results.note: Improves 35 of 45 languages (32 of 45 for English only); per-language average 77.2 vs 73.3

limits: LLM labels are noisy (89% human-checked accuracy, weaker on the consistent class); should be re-checked for new domains.
Labeling needs a 540B LLM over 1.4M summaries; resources not available to everyone.
Multilingual experiment covers 4 high-resource languages; trade-off between language coverage and label quality unexplored.
Data filtering to raise label accuracy did not help; reason only conjectured.
Human eval is 100 examples with one rater each. No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; hardware and compute not stated.
Teacher is not independent of FLAN training on NLI; test-set contamination of FLAN-PaLM not ruled out beyond noting FLAN instruction data is public.
